references.description: User-supplied 写真1.jpg: 3D wake, velocity section and grid-dependence chart. Reference for scientific visual vocabulary; not validated by this UI task.
Existing RocketWright analysis mockup: interface, water-bottle rocket, miniature workers.

generation_prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: one polished desktop web application screenshot for RocketWright, wide 16:9 landscape, Japanese interface, crisp product-design presentation.
Primary request: evolve the existing RocketWright dark analysis workspace by adding a large physical-looking widescreen analysis display BEHIND the tiny construction/maintenance characters and the real water-bottle rocket. The screen shows intermediate fluid-analysis outputs as they arrive. This backscreen is the defining visual feature, like an engineering workshop review screen.
Input images: Image 1 is the user's scientific analysis reference: a side view of a rocket in a translucent teal turbulent wake/velocity isosurface, below it a yellow/teal/blue velocity cross-section and a separate mesh-dependence line graph. Use this recognizable scientific visualization vocabulary, not its white page background or its numeric results. Image 2 is the established RocketWright UI master: neutral charcoal CAD-style shell, blue-nosed transparent water-bottle rocket, tiny gray-clothed workers wearing ochre safety helmets. Preserve product identity, worker design language, material quality, and calm neutral dark interface.
Layout: edge-to-edge app screenshot, no laptop/device, no browser chrome, no macOS traffic lights. Slim top app bar, narrow left analysis-stage dock (about 14% width), large central scene (about 69%), compact right live-results dock (about 17%), bottom progress/status area. Fine one-pixel dividers and compact rectangular controls, continuous panels. No floating bento cards, gradient marketing, meaningless sci-fi gauges.
Central scene: cinematic but restrained miniature engineering hangar on near-black background. A VERY LARGE landscape dark-framed monitor on a matte metal truss fills the upper and middle back wall and is perfectly legible. Its graphics are clear, dominant, not obscured by characters. On the monitor, top 65% is a beautifully detailed horizontally oriented rocket with blue nose at left, ochre fins and translucent ice-teal/cyan turbulent wake trailing right; fine gray grid and millimeter axes, subtle depth, no decorative HUD. Bottom 35% has TWO equally readable scientific panels: a velocity-section heatmap with proper continuous blue-to-teal-to-yellow legend captioned '速度断面', and a clean residual convergence plot with four differently colored lines, iterations on x-axis and residual on y-axis, captioned '残差'. Do NOT call the reference mesh-dependence graph a convergence plot: this is a separate proposed live residual chart. Header on physical monitor: '流体解析 / 正面風'. Small status '計算途中・未収束'. Quantitative values in this mock are illustrative; avoid a large authoritative drag coefficient or passed/verified badge.
Foreground scene: low raised work platform occupying lower central quarter. The same transparent PET water-bottle rocket with blue nose and blue fins lies horizontally on a practical small support cradle, nose left, matching the monitor's orientation. Three SMALL cute professional miniature workers, gray coveralls, ochre helmets: one by a fin with caliper, one with a tablet, one standing off to the side pointing toward the backscreen. One short platform/step and a compact tool trolley. They are charming but only a small part of the viewport; do not cover the visualization. Realistic soft shadows, matte metal, gentle warm work light and faint light from the monitor. The monitor remains the main focal point.
Exact UI copy (prioritize accurate Japanese and readable few labels):
Top left 'RocketWright', project 'water-rocket / 案A', top right small 'UIドラフト / 表示例' and a gear '設定'.
Left dock title '解析の工程'. Four stages: checked '条件の確認', selected '流体解析', queued '飛行と回収', queued '設計案の比較'. Under divider '解析対象' and '機体全体・フィン'. Lower compact '経過 02:18', 'この工程の残り 約1〜2分'.
Right dock title '途中結果'. Top small '案A · v12'. Three timestamped result rows '02:18  後流の3D表示', '02:06  速度断面', '01:54  残差グラフ'. Selected row is the latest. Under rows a compact switch '最新に追従' on, and a subtle button 'この結果を固定'. Short explanation '後流の変化を確認しています。' and '収束後に比較へ進みます。' Bottom buttons '動きを止める' and '解析を中断' visually separate. No chat bubbles needed in this mode.
Below central screen at scene bottom a slim snapshot ribbon with THREE tiny dark plot thumbnails and times '01:54', '02:06', '02:18', latest selected. Inline newest-state indicator '新しい途中結果'. Under ribbon stage status '流体解析を実行中' and '反復 240 / 上限 600' with subtext '収束条件で終了'. Upper-limit iterations are NOT a percentage complete; do not draw a fake 40% overall progress bar.
Style: faithful neutral charcoal CAD workbench, thin gray separators, white/dim gray Japanese sans serif, blue selected-stage accent and a few teal data accents only. Rich scientific graphics provide color. Sharp readable UI, coherent 3D scale and perspective, sophisticated engineering studio rather than a toy dashboard. Keep visual hierarchy calm, no excessive glow, no neon frames, no exaggerated smiling mascot faces. All results are a design mockup, not a claim to have run this simulation.
refinement_prompt: Edit this RocketWright UI mockup with one small consistency correction only. Preserve the entire image composition, resolution/aspect ratio, all Japanese interface labels, rocket, workers, rear screen, colors and scientific heatmap. In every residual plot (the lower-right plot on the large rear monitor, the right-side residual thumbnail, and the first thumbnail along the bottom), keep the iteration x-axis ending at 600 but truncate every plotted residual curve at iteration 240, leaving the interval 240 to 600 empty. The live counter is '反復 240 / 上限 600', so there must be no calculated residual samples beyond iteration 240. Do not change the counter or status '計算途中・未収束'. Make no other changes.
status: Static design proposal. Graphics, iteration counts, elapsed times and ETA are illustrative; no CFD run or runtime integration is claimed.
refinement: Truncated illustrative residual curves at the current iteration instead of extending them to the iteration limit.
